name: Reliance Industries Ltd
title: Reliance Industries Ltd - 500325 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Reliance Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA flat YoY as Oil-to-Chemicals fell 4%, while Jio and Retail grew 14% combined; FY26 EBITDA up 13.5%.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a quarter of severe energy shock from the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, with crude premiums, freight and insurance costs sharply higher and refinery throughput down 4% YoY to 19.5 MMT-equivalent (as stated). Consumer businesses (Jio and Retail) drove growth, with Jio Platforms FY26 EBITDA of Rs 76,255 Crores (around 19% YoY) and Retail record quarterly revenue of Rs 98,000 Crores. Quarterly PAT was pressured by higher depreciation and interest from 5G asset capitalisation. Management said Jio IPO is "fairly imminent" and gave no hard numbers on targets or margins beyond the stated trends.

financial_highlights.metric: Group FY26 EBITDA growth (includes one-time gain on sale of listed shares)

segments.name: Jio Platforms / Connectivity (RJIL)
segments.commentary: Ended FY26 with 524.4 mn subscribers (net add 9.1 mn in quarter); 268 mn 5G users (+77 mn in year); 27 mn fixed broadband homes, 75% via JioAirFiber. ARPU Rs 214, up 4% YoY with no tariff action; data per capita 42.3 GB/month.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Record Q4 revenue Rs 98,000 Crores (+11% YoY, ~14% ex-RCPL); EBITDA Rs 6,900 Crores at 7.9% margin, margin diluted by hyperlocal growth. Hyperlocal average daily orders +300% YoY; store count crossed 20,000 with 333 openings in the quarter.

segments.name: FMCG (Reliance Consumer Products)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 22,000 Crores; Q4 Rs 7,350 Crores, roughly 2x YoY. Campa brand Rs 4,700 Crores; Independence Rs 2,600 Crores; present in 40 countries; acquired Goodness Group (Australia) and Manna (millets).

segments.name: JioStar
segments.commentary: Monthly active user reach of 550 mn in March; T20 World Cup peak concurrency of 72.5 mn streams (record); linear TV share 34.7%; digital entertainment watch time +35%. TV ad revenue under pressure from FMCG spend cuts.

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (O2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA down 4% YoY; refinery throughput down 4% (FY26 19.5 vs 20.3 MMT). Gasoil crack averaged $35.4/bbl, ATF $36.3; gasoline crack $5.6. Downstream and polymer margins under pressure from elevated naphtha (up 13% YoY) and freight.

segments.name: Exploration & Production (KG-D6 / CBM)
segments.commentary: Production decline held to 8% vs 12-14% expected; Q4 EBITDA margin slightly lower on higher opex (asset integrity work, workovers). Gas price ceiling revised to about $8.9/MMBtu; CBM not subject to ceiling.

segments.name: New Energy
segments.commentary: Signed one of the world's largest green ammonia supply contracts with Samsung C&T. Targets 20 GW integrated solar/cell capacity and 100 GWh battery scaling; first 40 GWh BESS and cell phase commissioning in the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects cracks to remain strong for some time given refinery damage in the Middle East and shipping/insurance concerns; structurally tight refining market.
Customs duty exemption on key petrochemicals valid to end of Q1 FY27; likely to be revoked in Q2 if prices moderate.
Jio IPO described as 'fairly imminent'; DRHP timing not given.
Retail square footage and store count expected to grow; no numeric guidance given.
Management expects Jio ARPU to rise 4-5% organically without tariff hikes; digital services to grow faster than connectivity from a smaller base.
Two large O2C projects (vinyl and PTA) prioritised for accelerated execution.
capex_capacity: Jamnagar green hydrogen/ammonia trains in detailed engineering and fabrication; Kutch 12 land parcels (5.3 lakh acres) under development; Kutch-Lakadia and Kutch-Jamnagar transmission EPC awarded.

Giga factories: module and cell lines commissioned with ALMM listing (first HJT lines in India); polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell and glass commissioning targeted in next few quarters; integrated capacity 20 GW.
Battery scaling to 100 GWh with equipment orders placed; first 40 GWh BESS/cell phase commissioning during the year.
Gigawatt-scale AI data centres being worked on; progress updates expected in next few quarters.
E&P: rig for MGA field expected later this year; 40 multilateral CBM wells planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic fuel demand FY26: gasoline +6.5%, diesel +3.6%; Q4 domestic demand grew 2.7% YoY with gasoline +7%, diesel +5%, ATF +3%.
RBML (retail JV) volume growth ~27% YoY; 50-60 outlets added QoQ; CBG/CNG volumes +65%.
Naphtha price up 13% YoY; PE/PP demand +3%, PVC -10% (pipe-grade imports disrupted), polyester chain +16% on paraxylene strength.
Asian naphtha crackers ethylene operating rates fell from 80% to 60% during the disruption; Saudi OSP premium reportedly $20-30/bbl.
Retail LFL growth mid-to-high single digits; grocery and fashion posted double-digit growth; Ajio Luxe brand portfolio +24%; Jewels AOV +53%.
Jio: 5G users 54% of mobility consumers; monthly churn declining.

qa_highlights.question: How much could distillate yield change if refinery runs rely on alternate crudes (US, Africa, Venezuela) with different sulphur and gravity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the refinery is designed for heavy crudes and processes 200+ grades; Venezuelan re-entry is a positive, and Urals is a Middle East look-alike, so composition is not seen as a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fuel retail business handling losses, and is there a price-increase trigger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail sales grew 20% or more YoY with ~4-5% market share; it will keep domestic supply without curtailment and take a long-term view, with PSUs bearing most of the under-recovery burden.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for crude premiums, freight and cracks?
qa_highlights.answer: Situation is fluid: cracks have cooled, and crude premiums that reached about $40/bbl are now around half that; management expects refining to stay structurally strong.

qa_highlights.question: Which products are affected by SAED?
qa_highlights.answer: Only diesel is materially affected in the domestic-focused DTA refinery output; jet is negligible, and the impact is a discount in the domestic channel.

qa_highlights.question: Retail growth decomposition: SSSG vs square footage vs quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RCPL demerger cut reported growth by ~3 pp; SSSG offline is healthy single digit; QC and B2B are ramping and pressuring margins. Declined to give a square footage growth number, only that it will grow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JPL EBITDA rise faster than revenue, and when is the Jio IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin gain to operating leverage, as delivery costs did not rise with new contracts; IPO is 'fairly imminent' with no DRHP timing given. AI data centres sit in the intelligence entity, not JPL.

qa_highlights.question: What would success look like for Jio in terms of ROIC or FCF over 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give financial targets, citing priorities of mobility share, homes, enterprise and digital services scaling.

risks_watch: Crude supply and freight: refinery throughput fell to 19.5 MMT in FY26 from 20.3 MMT as Middle East supply was disrupted; management says cracks may stay strong but the situation is fluid.

Policy and regulatory exposure: SAED introduced effective 27 March 2026 hits domestic diesel; customs duty exemption on key petrochemicals runs to end Q1 FY27 and is likely to be revoked in Q2; fuel under-recoveries remain with retail.
Retail margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin at 7.9% as hyperlocal and quick commerce grow; management gave no timeline for margin stability and no square footage growth number.
Jio IPO timing: described as fairly imminent but no DRHP timing; earlier first-half 2026 expectation not confirmed on the call.
E&P decline and gas pricing: KG-D6 decline held at 8% but the gas ceiling price was revised to about $8.9/MMBtu, and the Qatar LNG outage affects Indian gas supply.
Petchem demand and feedstock: naphtha up 13% YoY, PVC demand down 10%, Asian cracker operating rates fell from 80% to 60%; vinyl and PTA mega-projects need timely execution.
key_quotes: Now, with the consumer businesses contributing more than 55% of EBITDA and PAT growth was also good
So, the situation is very fluid. Nobody really knows what is going to happen.
It is fairly imminent. We are working towards it, and we will keep you posted.
I am not going to put numbers to where we want to be in one or two years.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on consumer businesses (Jio, Retail, JioStar, FMCG) and on refining resilience, citing record Retail revenue and strong subscriber metrics. It was cautious and evasive on fuel-retail losses, the Q1 crude and freight outlook ("the situation is very fluid"), IPO timing and Jio financial targets, declining to give numbers on each.

adds.what: Giga factories: module and cell lines commissioned (first HJT lines in India); integrated solar capacity target 20 GW
First 40 GWh BESS/cell phase of battery scaling (toward 100 GWh)

growth.why: No numeric group revenue guidance; consumer businesses (Jio EBITDA +18-19% FY26, Retail revenue +11% Q4) and new energy build-out (giga factory lines, 40 GWh BESS in phases) back growth, but Q4 group EBITDA was flat and O2C EBITDA fell 4% amid the energy shock, and most capacity timelines are not numerically specified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Jio margin rose 190 bps to 52% FY26 and RJIL Q4 margin rose 230 bps to 56.2% on operating leverage, offset by Retail Q4 margin at 7.9% diluted by hyperlocal and quick commerce and O2C pressure from naphtha and freight; no margin-stability timeline was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Giga factory module and cell lines already commissioned, 40 GWh BESS first phase under construction and polysilicon/ingot/wafer/cell/glass commissioning targeted in the next few quarters, toward 20 GW integrated solar capacity; E&P rig for MGA later this year and 40 CBM wells planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Jio added 9.1 mn subscribers in Q4 to 524.4 mn with 5G users up 77 mn to 268 mn; RBML volumes +27% YoY, CBG/CNG volumes +65%, and Retail LFL growth is mid-to-high single digit; domestic fuel demand grew 2.7% in Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Refinery was run close to capacity but throughput fell 4% to 19.5 MMT in FY26 and no utilisation % was given; gigawatt-scale AI data centres and Kutch 12 land (5.3 lakh acres) progress updates are expected in the next few quarters, but no new refinery capex was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects cracks to stay strong for some time given Middle East refinery damage (gasoil crack averaged $35.4/bbl, ATF $36.3), but cracks have already cooled and crude premiums of about $40/bbl have halved, so upside depends on the situation staying tight.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 group EBITDA was flat YoY with O2C EBITDA down 4% on naphtha up 13% and SAED hitting domestic diesel; customs duty exemption on petchem ends Q1 FY27 and is likely revoked in Q2 if prices moderate, and management said the Q1 outlook is 'very fluid'.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First HJT module and cell lines already commissioned, first 40 GWh BESS/cell phase commissioning during the year, and Retail store count crossed 20,000 with 333 openings in the quarter.

rows.label: Jio Platforms IPO
rows.why: Management called the IPO 'fairly imminent' with JPL FY26 PAT above Rs 30,000 Crores and Q4 PAT of Rs 7,935 Crores, but no DRHP timing was given and the earlier first-half 2026 expectation was not confirmed.

rows.label: Jio ARPU rise without tariff hikes
rows.why: ARPU was Rs 214 (+4% YoY) with no tariff action, and management expects a further 4-5% organic rise, with monthly churn declining.

rows.label: Petchem customs duty exemption revocation
rows.why: Duty exemption on key petrochemicals runs to end Q1 FY27 and is likely to be revoked in Q2 if prices moderate, which would weigh on O2C feedstock economics.

tone.note: Management was confident on Jio, Retail, JioStar, FMCG and refining resilience, but cautious and evasive on fuel-retail losses, Q1 crude and freight outlook, IPO timing and Jio financial targets, declining to give numbers.
